transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Jonas Li (Redwood SE); Laura Kim (Aegis - Head of ML); Derek O'Neal (Aegis - Platform Eng); Priya Rao (Aegis - Security); Tom Nguyen (Aegis - Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be edited): Align on POC scope, benchmarks (latency/cost/quality), network access plan (VPC peering), timeline for kickoff -> midpoint -> exec readout, and responsibilities.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate squeezing this in during the holidays. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Laura (Aegis): Laura here.
[00:08] Derek (Aegis): Derek, yep.
[00:10] Priya (Aegis): Priya here.
[00:12] Tom (Aegis): Tom on.
[00:14] Samir (Redwood SE): Samir as well.
[00:16] Jonas (Redwood SE): Jonas here.
[00:18] Maya: Great. Objective for today is tight: agree success criteria, make sure we understand the workload shape, what we need for access, and the milestone dates for the POC. I'll run quick overview, Samir will cover benchmark approach, then we can triage networking and security items.

[02:05] Maya: Quick context for the group: Aegis wants to validate a user-facing LLM feature for customer support triage — short responses, usually 40-80 tokens, lots of concurrency during end-of-day runs, and a long-tail of larger context for conversation history. Correct me if I’m off.
[02:28] Laura: That's right. The key is latency and cost per resolved ticket. If latency spikes above ~450 ms for the 95th percentile for short responses, product will object.
[02:40] Tom: Also want to measure hallucination rate on the triage prompts — we have a small set of labeled cases to test precision vs recall.

[03:20] Samir: Understood. For benchmarking we'll separate three buckets: short single-turn responses (40-80 tokens), mult-turn with KV cache usage (longer contexts), and batch re-ranking jobs. Each has different ideal batching and quantization profiles.
[03:52] Derek: Rough QPS expectation? Peak concurrency around 120 simultaneous requesters during business close, baseline 20 QPS steady state.
[04:05] Jonas: So if we plan for 120 concurrent low-latency requests, we'd recommend a dedicated pod configuration for the POC to avoid noisy neighbor effects. But we can simulate on hosted if you prefer.

[05:15] Laura: We're leaning toward private deployment (VPC) for this POC — data sensitivity, PII concerns. We want both performance guarantees and no customer data leaving VPC.
[05:30] Priya: Security will need SOC2 docs and details about KMS integration. Also curious about audit logs retention and RBAC.

[06:05] Maya: Noted. We'll share SOC2 and the security primer. For KMS we support bringing-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS — we'll document the flow.

[06:30] Samir: On success criteria — propose a short list we can gate on: 1) 95p latency < 450 ms for 40-80 token responses at 120 concurrent, 2) Cost per resolved ticket < $0.015 (token + infra amortized), 3) Hallucination rate < 2% on labeled set, 4) Throughput for batch rerank of 50k documents under X minutes. We can tune those numbers once Aegis provides labeled set and traffic profile.

[07:22] Laura: Hallucination target seems reasonable. Cost target might be aggressive; we'll need the benchmark template to map tokens and avg tokens per request.
[07:40] Maya: We'll send a benchmark template that has fields for avg tokens, peak concurrency, percentile latency, and cost calc. That will let us model different quantization profiles.

[09:05] Derek: Networking — what do you need from us to get VPC setup? Peering? Transit? We use AWS account X, accounts per environment.
[09:18] Jonas: We'll need a VPC peering or VPC endpoint. For POC we support peering + IAM roles to provision. We also have an option to run a private agent in your VPC that talks to Redwood control plane over an outbound-only connection — that sometimes simplifies compliance.
[09:45] Derek: Outbound-only sounds simpler for us, but we'll check with cloud ops. What's the latency tradeoff?
[09:53] Samir: Outbound-only introduces a slight additional hop but typically under 10-15 ms added RTT. For your 95p budget that's okay; the bigger factors are batching and model size.

[11:30] Priya: For auditability we need logs shipped to our SIEM and immutable audit logs for inference requests. Can Redwood emit structured logs and a stream to S3 or our account?
[11:45] Maya: Yes — we can stream logs and provide token-level cost breakdowns. We'll include an example JSON schema in the security packet.

[12:20] Tom: Timeline — what's realistic? We want kickoff ASAP, but need internal signoffs. Can we aim for a Jan-early kickoff?
[12:33] Maya: If we get access by Jan 6, a 4-week POC is doable: week 0 = access + baseline runs, week 1-2 tunings & integrations, week 3 = mid-point readout, week 4 = final exec readout.
[12:50] Laura: That aligns. We prefer a mid-point readout at about week 3 to demonstrate traction.

[14:00] Samir: For benchmarks we'll run scripted loads using your prompt set and an internal harness. We'll produce: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokens consumed, cost estimate, and quality metrics (F1/precision/recall for labelled set). We'll also run a gating checklist for regression detection.

[15:10] Derek: For the harness, what credentials or endpoints will we need?
[15:18] Jonas: We'll provide an S3-compatible bucket for log collection and a small docker image that your ops can run in a bastion to push metrics back to our collector. For private deployments we'll give a signed cert for the agent.

[16:05] Priya: Can you also include data retention options? We can't keep raw transcripts longer than X days in our test environment.
[16:13] Maya: Yes, retention is configurable per route. We'll document retention and anonymization options.

[17:30] Laura: On success criteria ownership — who will be the single point from Redwood to own benchmark runs and attestation?
[17:38] Maya: Samir will be primary for the bench runs and Jonas will handle infra and setup. I'll be the commercial lead.

[18:05] Samir: Also recommend a small smoke test before mid-point: run 1 hour at 60 concurrence to validate perf and logs, then do full peak simulation.

[19:20] Tom: For the labeled set for hallucination checks — we have 500 labeled samples. We can share a sanitized CSV.
[19:30] Laura: We'll also include edge-case examples and weighted importance per class.

[20:50] Maya: Good. Two gating rules to propose: 1) Technical gate: benchmark results meet threshold (latency & quality), 2) Ops gate: production-like observability and secure KMS integration validated. If both pass, we move to exec readout.

[21:30] Derek: What happens if the latency gate fails but quality is good? Do we consider fallbacks like a smaller model or increasing concurrency?
[21:40] Samir: We can propose a hybrid routing policy — route critical short responses to a lower-latency quantized model, route long-context to higher-accuracy variant. For POC we'll prototype routing rules.

[23:00] Priya: Regarding KMS BYOK — does Redwood support AWS KMS and other providers? We use AWS KMS with CloudHSM.
[23:10] Jonas: Yes, AWS KMS is supported; we have a documented KMS integration flow and can validate access with a temporary key for the POC.

[24:12] Maya: Let's capture concrete dates: action items — Maya will share the benchmark template by Jan 4; Derek to open peering ticket Jan 3; Priya to share compliance doc list Jan 5. Kickoff scheduled if access is ready on Jan 6; midpoint readout tentatively Jan 27; exec readout Feb 3. Does that timeline work?
[24:48] Laura: Dates OK as tentative. We may shift the exec readout one week depending on QA availability.

[26:00] Tom: One more ask — cost transparency in the readout. Can you show the cost drivers and how quantization/batching affects unit economics?
[26:12] Samir: Yes — our perf spreadsheet will include config toggles (batch size, quantization level, KV cache hit rate) and show ballpark costs per 1k requests so you can see trade-offs.

[28:00] Maya: Any competitor concerns? Laura?
[28:08] Laura: We'll be benchmarking against Anthropic results and also some internal GPU infra runs. Want to ensure apples-to-apples.

[29:10] Samir: We'll align the harness so you can run the same prompts against other providers and submit results into the same template. Helps fairness.

[30:30] Jonas: Quick note — for private deployments we may need a short maintenance window for image pull and key exchange; we'll coordinate with Derek.

[31:40] Priya: Audit requirement — encryption in transit + at rest, and an immutable request log for 90 days for the POC.
[31:50] Maya: We'll include that in the security packet.

[33:05] Laura: Regarding success criteria, can we make a small matrix that ties business KPI to benchmark metrics? E.g., resolved ticket time -> p95 latency; CSAT proxy -> hallucination rate.
[33:20] Maya: Absolutely; we'll draft that mapping and include it with the benchmark template.

[34:55] Samir: On workload sizing, we estimate per-request token consumption and average response time; if you can fill token profiles for sample payloads we can finalize required GPU footprints. For 120 concurrent short requests we expect to use 2-3 gpus in a dedicated config depending on quantization.

[36:10] Derek: If we go hosted versus private what are the differences in the POC scope?
[36:18] Maya: Hosted is faster to start, but you won't get VPC isolation or BYOK. Private gives full network control and BYOK but needs slightly more setup. Both can run the same bench harness; results are comparable but private avoids egress concerns.

[38:00] Tom: Ok. For exec readout content — we want a short deck: objective, baseline metrics, improvements/tuning done, cost implications, and next recommended rollout steps.

[38:15] Maya: We'll produce that deck as part of the readout + a detailed appendix with raw benchmark CSVs.

[39:30] Laura: Anything else on timeline?
[39:34] Derek: One more on roles — Derek will act as cloud ops contact; Priya will be security approver; Laura will sign off technical success; Tom will evaluate product fit.

[40:00] Maya: Great. Recap of immediate next steps: share benchmark template (Maya), open networking ticket (Derek), security doc list (Priya), share labeled set (Laura).

[41:20] Samir: We'll also prepare a small smoke test plan and checklist to run once access is provided.

[42:00] Laura: Sounds good — appreciate the clarity.

[46:00] Maya: Any last questions?
[46:05] Tom: None here.
[46:10] Priya: Nothing further.

[47:00] Maya: Thanks, team. We'll follow up with the templates and calendar invites for kickoff.
